title: Rate limits are keyed per action-and-asset pair, so caps bound each venue-asset conduit rather than aggregate exposure
content:
The rate-limit key is constructed, not global: `RateLimitHelpers.makeAssetKey(LIMIT_AAVE_DEPOSIT, aToken)` (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.2.1.3.1.3) and `RateLimitHelpers.makeAssetKey(LIMIT_AAVE_WITHDRAW, aToken)` (.3.2.3). The limit identity is therefore the pair (action, asset), and the instance documents confirm this by publishing separate inflow and outflow `RateLimitID`s for the same conduit (.1.6.2.3.1 and .1.6.2.3.2 hold two different hashes).

Granularity per conduit is what makes the limits useful — an incident in one venue-asset pairing should not consume the capacity of an unrelated one, and each limit can be sized against that venue's specific liquidity and risk profile.

The consequence is that no documented number in this chunk bounds total deployment. SparkLend alone shows inflow ceilings of 100,000,000 USDC, 100,000,000 DAI, 500,000,000 USDT, 100,000,000 pyUSD and 50,000 ETH, each with its own independently refilling slope. Nothing in these documents prevents them being drawn concurrently, so the effective aggregate inflow capacity is the sum of the parts, refreshed in parallel.

An aggregate constraint may well exist elsewhere in the Spark Artifact or in the Allocation System Primitive, but a reader who reasons about total risk from instance-level `maxAmount` values will systematically understate it. The per-conduit design optimises for containment of a single venue failure, not for bounding total balance-sheet deployment.
description: RateLimitHelpers.makeAssetKey(LIMIT_AAVE_DEPOSIT, aToken) derives a distinct limit per aToken, meaning simultaneous draws across instances can sum well above any single documented maxAmount.
